title: Stop-Service and Final Billing Rule — Final Bills, Refunds and Closing Electric Service by Rate Schedule Accounts
content:
**Final billing.** An Electric Service by Rate Schedule account is final billed on the requested date of the member's confirmed stop-service order or, for an account disconnected for nonpayment, once the schedule's finaling period, in calendar days, has passed since the disconnect date. The final bill carries the usage to the final read and a full facility charge.

**Deposits and capital credits.** A security deposit held on the account is applied to the final bill under the Security Deposits rules. Capital credits are never applied to a final bill until the board retires them under Capital Credits (Patronage Capital).

**Final credit balance.** A final credit balance of at least the schedule's check refund minimum is refunded by check to the mailing address on file within 30 calendar days of the final bill; a smaller one is refunded only on the member's request.

**Closing.** An account is closed only when its account balance is exactly zero. An unpaid final balance stays on the final-billed account and blocks new service for the member under the cooperative's unpaid final balance policy.

### Outcomes after the final bill (hypothetical, $5.00 check refund minimum)

| Balance after the final bill and any deposit application | Result |
|---|---|
| $0.00 | Account closed |
| Credit of $18.40 | Refunded by check within 30 calendar days of the final bill |
| Credit of $3.10 | Refunded only if the member asks |
| $46.75 owed | Stays final billed; the member cannot open new service until it is paid |

### Finaling period — hypothetical

A Schedule GS-1 account (finaling period 14 calendar days) disconnected for nonpayment on April 2 becomes due for final billing once 14 calendar days have passed since April 2.
